title: RBAC v2 + Audit-log Export: Control Mapping, Gap Analysis, and Auditor Cue Cards
content:
Purpose:
This working playbook is intended to help the security and compliance team quickly assemble mapped evidence for external SOC 2 and ISO 27001 auditors related to RBAC v2, our audit log schema, and SIEM export automation. It contains: a concise control mapping, a focused gap analysis with mitigations and owners, and short interviewer cue-cards and sample artifacts to present during an audit call.

Scope:
- RBAC v2 product changes (grant model, role inheritance, resource-scoped roles)
- Audit log schema (user identity, actor metadata, request lifecycle, response codes, KV for resource ids)
- Evidence automation and SIEM export pipeline (Kafka -> SIEM ingestion -> retention/archival)
- Mapping to SOC 2 common criteria and ISO/IEC 27001 controls referenced by auditors most often for access control and logging.

Executive summary (one paragraph):
RBAC v2 introduces resource-scoped role assignments and delegation, improving least-privilege semantics. We emit structured audit events (json-lines) enriched with identity provider (IdP) assertions, role delta diffs, and request routing metadata. SIEM exports run through a validated pipeline that provides immutable sequences, chainable offsets, and automated evidence bundles for retention windows. Current risks are primarily around demonstrable retention proof for filtered exports, and automated test coverage for cross-tenant access-change events. The mitigations below prioritize reproducible evidence and small, auditable playbooks for demoing to auditors.

Control mapping (high-level):
- SOC 2: Logical and physical access controls (Common Criteria / CC6) => RBAC v2 enforces role-based access; evidence: role assignment records, approval workflow logs, access review tickets; audit logs: "access.change" events with before/after role payloads.
- SOC 2: System operations and availability (CC5/CC7) => SIEM export and ingestion health metrics, delivery acknowledgements (Kafka offsets), alert history for export failures.
- ISO 27001: A.9 Access control => role definitions, provisioning/deprovisioning flows, proof of privileged role approval (ticket links + signed attestations).
- ISO 27001: A.12 Operations security => logging and monitoring requirements satisfied by immutable audit stream and SIEM retention policy; evidence: immutable archive manifest, retention config.

Detailed RBAC -> Control traces (short bullets):
- Feature: Resource-scoped roles (roleBinding.resource_id + roleRef)
  - SOC2 trace: access.records/role_binding.json (sample export) -> shows who granted role, approver (if approval required), timestamp, and TTL.
  - ISO27001 trace: A.9.1.2 mapping in access-control-matrix (Confluence page) + provisioning ticket.
- Feature: Role inheritance and delegations
  - SOC2 trace: role.evaluation.trace entries in logs that show effective-roles calculation for a session.
  - ISO27001 trace: periodic access review artifacts (spreadsheet of effective-roles exported from API with hashes).
- Feature: Admin-initiated role changes (console and API)
  - Trace: admin.audit.events with request_id and sys_user_id; retention-proof exported to SIEM index redwood-rbac-admin-YYYY.MM.DD.

Audit log schema (important fields to highlight for auditors):
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- event_type (rbac.role_assigned | rbac.role_revoked | auth.login | auth.token_refresh | request.start | request.end)
- actor_id (internal user id)
- actor_external_id (idp:user@example.com)
- role_before (list)
- role_after (list)
- resource_id
- request_id (correlation id across services)
- outcome (success | failure | partial)
- reason (optional free text, usually populated for denials or manual changes)
- signature (HMAC of event payload for immutability)
Note: auditors typically look for immutable timestamps, stable identifiers, and linkage from role changes to an approver or ticket. Have a sample event (sanitized) ready.

SIEM export and evidence automation (current design):
1) Producer: unified audit-log-producer streams json-lines to Kafka topic audit.events.v2 (partitioned by tenant_id).
2) Router: streaming enrichment service consumes, adds identity assertions and signature, writes to compact S3 archive and also forwards to SIEM-specific topic.
3) Exporter: SIEM connector (Logstash/Fluent) consumes and posts to vendor SIEM index with delivery confirmation stored as meta-record (kafka offsets + s3 manifest path).
4) Retention/archival: daily compaction job creates immutable manifests (signed) and copies to cold storage for 7 years (policy).
5) Evidence bundle: automation job that given a tenant_id + date-range packages logs, manifest, and hash-signed index and creates a downloadable artifact with an audit trail (ticket id, operator, run id).

Gap analysis (concise, action-focused):
1) Gap: Incomplete documented proof that SIEM export retains original event signatures after transformation.
   - Impact: Auditor cannot verify immutability after our enrichment step.
   - Mitigation: Add signature propagation field original_signature; produce test vectors demonstrating identical HMAC inputs pre- and post-export. Owner: Mateo. Jira: JIRA-SEC-4899. Target: 2024-12-20.
2) Gap: Lack of canned auditor-ready sample of cross-tenant role-eval (effective role) for combined console + API change sequence.
   - Impact: During live walkthroughs we rely on ad-hoc queries which slows audit calls.
   - Mitigation: Create a synthetic tenant demo script that performs a role grant -> evaluation -> access attempt -> evidence bundle. Owner: Jordan. Jira: JIRA-SEC-4931. Target: 2024-11-30.
3) Gap: Export retention proof for filtered SIEM extracts (we currently export using tenant_id filtering but don't attach filter manifests).
   - Impact: Auditor may question whether excluded events were discarded or just not exported.
   - Mitigation: Add export-filter-manifest to every bundle documenting exact query predicates + pre-export counts + post-export counts. Owner: Evelyn. Jira: JIRA-SEC-4922. Target: 2024-12-10.

Evidence artifacts to prepare (quick checklist for auditor meeting):
- Access control policy doc (Confluence link) and signed change log.
- Sample role_binding export for 3 demo tenants (JSON, sanitized).
- One full audit event (raw) with signature proof and S3 manifest showing same event preserved.
- SIEM export manifest showing offsets and hashes for the day's export.
- Retention policy and archival proof (cold storage manifest).
- Playbook run log for evidence bundle creation (ticket id and run id).
- Access review meeting notes and attestation emails for privileged role changes in the last 6 months.

Auditor cue-cards (short interviewer Q&A with suggested artifacts to table):
- Q: How do you ensure only authorized users can grant privileged roles?
  - Cue: Show role grant approval workflow diagram (Confluence), demo role_binding JSON with approver_id, and ticket JIRA-OPS-3214 where approval is captured.
- Q: How are role change events linked back to identity provider assertions?
  - Cue: Show a raw event including actor_external_id + idp_assertion fields, then show the enrichment pipeline step that appends idp assertions.
- Q: Can you prove an event hasn't been altered after export?
  - Cue: Present the original_signature on the event and the s3 manifest with hash chain; run the signature verification script (link in Confluence).
- Q: How do you demonstrate retention and disposition of logs?
  - Cue: Show retention policy doc, S3 lifecycle rules screenshot, and last archival manifest.
- Q: What happens on SIEM export failures?
  - Cue: Show alert history, remediation playbook link and a sample incident ticket where export retried successfully.

Live demo script (5–7 minutes, high level):
- Step 0: Pre-step: create evidence bundle job for demo-tenant-123 for last 24h; have the bundle id ready.
- Step 1: In console, create a temporary role grant to a test user (RBAC v2 UI).
- Step 2: Trigger evaluation API to show effective roles.
- Step 3: Attempt an action that should be allowed by new role (show success).
- Step 4: Present the audit event stream (filter by request_id) and show before/after role arrays + signature.
- Step 5: Open evidence bundle; show s3 manifest, signature verification, and SIEM export manifest for the same request_id.

Automation runbook (lean steps for evidence bundle creation):
1) Run: ./scripts/build_evidence_bundle.sh --tenant demo-tenant-123 --from 2024-11-01 --to 2024-11-02 --reason "auditor-review"
2) The script provisions a temporary query job (query id returned), compacts the results to s3://evidence-bundles/<bundle-id> and produces bundle.json with fields: {bundle_id, tenant_id, from, to, manifest_path, created_by, created_at}.
3) Confirm manifest signature: ./tools/verify_manifest.sh s3://evidence-bundles/<bundle-id>/manifest.json
4) Attach bundle id to the audit ticket and share time-limited download link.

Suggested artifacts filenames (examples):
- demo-tenant-123-role-binding-2024-11-01.json
- audit-event-req-0a1b2c3d.json (signed)
- evidence-bundle-demo-tenant-123-20241101.tar.gz
- siem-export-manifest-2024-11-01.json

Next steps (action items before next auditor call):

- [ ] Jordan: create synthetic demo script and upload demo tenant artifacts to evidence-bundles. (JIRA-SEC-4931)
- [ ] Evelyn: implement export-filter-manifest and include pre/post counts in bundles. (JIRA-SEC-4922)
- [ ] Anya: draft a 1-page handout for auditors summarizing mapping table and demo script. (due 2024-11-22)

Appendix A — sample sanitized audit event (for demo):
{"timestamp":"2024-11-14T16:23:07Z","event_type":"rbac.role_assigned","actor_id":"u-0459","actor_external_id":"anya.patel@redwood.ai","role_before":[],"role_after":["dedicated.viewer"],"resource_id":"gpu-pool-23","request_id":"req-0a1b2c3d","outcome":"success","signature":"sha256:abcdef123456..."}

Appendix B — quick references:
- Confluence: RBAC v2 design + schema (linked_artifacts above)
- Repo: platform/audit-producer (PR 987 contains enrichment changes)
- Jira: JIRA-SEC-4899, JIRA-SEC-4922, JIRA-SEC-4931

Notes & discussion points (for internal reviewers):
- Keep the demo artifacts sanitized: never include real PII or tenant-sensitive names in shared bundles.
- Where possible, prepare both console and API traces so auditors can validate both UI and API paths.
- Be ready to run the verify_manifest script during the call — practice once with platform team.

End of document.
__notes: Working draft playbook for audit prep. Contains live action items and owners.
